thesis.core: The two core businesses are growing, the light-conveyor segment shows improving domestic profitability, the balance sheet remains strong and shareholder payout is meaningful; however, current valuation already captures most of the normalized earnings recovery.
thesis.variant_wedge: H1 headline cash conversion looks weak, but a large tax prepayment and inventory/order timing explain part of the decline. Even after normalizing those effects and allowing for FX relief, the equity does not clear a 15% new-capital hurdle at RMB4.30.
thesis.normalized_earnings_basis: Use 2026E normalized EPS bear/base/bull of RMB0.24/RMB0.30/RMB0.36, anchored to H1 EPS RMB0.1411, H1 deduct EPS about RMB0.134, FX losses, segment mix and a second-half normalization assumption.

financial_quality.judgment: Earnings are stable rather than fast-growing; cash conversion is temporarily depressed but not fully explained by deterioration, while net assets and cash provide downside support.

operating_detail.judgment: Domestic conveyor profitability is improving, while precision molding is being held back by FX; the Kunshan project adds medium-term growth optionality but also raises execution and ROIC requirements.

normalized_earnings_basis.rationale: H1 EPS was RMB0.1411; scenarios normalize FX, tax timing and second-half mix without assuming a structural margin step-up.

catalysts: FX losses normalize or are better contained through pricing and hedging, allowing revenue growth to translate into profit growth.
Light-conveyor domestic margin improvement persists as automation/logistics demand and high-value products scale.
Operating cash conversion normalizes after tax-prepayment and working-capital timing effects.
The Kunshan intelligent-transmission project ramps toward 2027 commissioning with credible returns on capital.
kill_thesis: Operating cash flow remains materially below normalized profit after temporary tax and working-capital effects reverse.
Precision-molding margins continue to decline even after FX normalization.
Kunshan or other expansion capex fails to produce acceptable ROIC or materially weakens the balance sheet.
The high shareholder payout proves unsustainable as growth capex and working capital rise.
